text:
maria_sales: Hey team — doing a POC with a customer on PrivateDeploy. They're streaming model responses up to ~20min and worried about NAT/firewall conntrack timeouts. What should we tell them for preflight? 

devin_se: PrivateLink terminates at the endpoint so the link itself doesn't expire, but middleboxes do. Many corporate firewalls evict idle TCP after 5–10m. If the stream is mostly server->client you need keepalives <60s or extend conntrack timers. 

ashok_netops: Key Qs: is traffic truly idle for long stretches? Are they doing source-IP preservation or is there a NAT/proxy before the endpoint? :thinking_face: 

maria_sales: It's mostly one-way (tokens from server) with the client sending keepalive pings every 30s. They prefer source IP preserved for audit logs. 

leah_sre: 30s keepalives should be fine for most appliances, but conntrack eviction under load is still possible. Recommend both network-level timeouts and app-level heartbeat. 

devin_se: Our standard customer guidance: 1) allowlist PrivateLink endpoint CIDR and connector egress IPs on 443/TCP; 2) increase TCP established conntrack timeout to >=1800s for streaming workloads; 3) send app keepalives <=60s. Want a short sample snippet we can share? 

ashok_netops: Linux NAT example — extend established timeout to 30 minutes:

```bash
# immediate
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=1800
# make persistent: add to /etc/sysctl.conf
``` 

ashok_netops: On Palo Alto/Check Point/F5 you'll need to adjust the per-connection idle timer (Palo Alto: "tcp-timeout" for established flows; F5: virtual-server idle; Check Point: per-connection timeout). Recommend engaging perimeter FW admins. 

maria_sales: Do we need to do anything on Redwood side? Customer asked if we can avoid session breaks during failover. 

jordan_product: No infra changes from our side. If we reroute to fallback region or model the TCP/TLS session will drop. Recommend application-level resume strategies: short logical sessions, idempotency tokens, resume offsets, or storing state externally (S3/Redis) so reconnects can continue. We can provide a tech note link. 

leah_sre: Also suggest client retry windows (~10s) and rehydrate KV cache on reconnect. Many customers implement resume semantics for long streams. 

maria_sales: Security: do we log client source IPs if PrivateLink is used? 

jordan_product: If the client IP is preserved (no NAT before endpoint) we will see it on the connector and it can show up in connect metadata. We primarily surface endpoint IP + connector instance ID in Console; payloads are not persisted. Recommend referencing our SOC/KMS docs and advising customer to use customer-managed KMS for sensitive workloads. 

secbot: Security checklist: for PII-sensitive workloads use customer-managed KMS for PrivateDeploy, enable audit logs, and rotate keys per policy. :lock: 

maria_sales: Can we produce a one-pager for the customer with recommended firewall timeouts, keepalive guidance, source-IP note, and failover behavior? Also include iptables + Palo Alto snippets. CC @ashok_netops for review. 

devin_se: I'll draft EOD. Summary to include:
- TCP conntrack established >= 1800s
- App keepalives <= 60s (30s preferred)
- Allowlist PrivateLink destination CIDR and connector egress IPs on 443/TCP
- Avoid NAT before PrivateLink if source-IP preservation is required
- Expect session break on active model/region failover; implement resume/retry

ashok_netops: Happy to review the snippets before send. 

maria_sales: Thanks — this should unblock the POC security signoff. :tada:
